extraction.name: RoboFAC
extraction.description: A large-scale dataset for robotic failure analysis and correction comprising 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories and 78,623 video question-answer pairs across 16 diverse tasks and 53 scenes in both simulation and real-world environments. The dataset categorizes robotic failures into six types across three hierarchical levels: task planning error, motion planning error, and execution control error.
extraction.creator: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao
extraction.publisher: School of AI, Shanghai Jiao Tong University
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed through a combination of simulation and real-world data collection. Simulation data was collected in the ManiSkill environment with augmented objects from YCB Object Dataset and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR. Expert policies were defined by specifying target end-effector poses, with motion planning generating feasible paths. Failure data was generated by replacing expert policies with code snippets that produce erroneous trajectories. Real-world data was collected via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm. Each video was recorded with corresponding descriptive text including substage information, failure taxonomy, and detailed error explanations. Manual data cleaning was performed, retaining approximately 75% of collected simulation data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Manual data cleaning was performed to remove trajectories that did not align with textual descriptions due to motion planning failures, retaining approximately 75% of collected data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of robotic failure videos and successful trajectories from both simulation and real-world environments. Simulation data includes 8,960 failure trajectories and 1,160 successful trajectories collected from 14 tasks in ManiSkill environment. Real-world data includes 480 failure trajectories and 122 successful trajectories from 6 tasks collected via teleoperation. Each video is accompanied by descriptive text including substage information, failure taxonomy, and detailed error explanations.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Eight question types were annotated using question templates (five templates per type). For five question types (task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, failure locating), reference answers were directly extracted from textual descriptions. For three question types (failure explanation, high-level correction, low-level correction), GPT-4o generated reference answers using video and textual description inputs, with manual review and correction for quality assurance.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All outputs from GPT-4o were manually reviewed and corrected to ensure annotation quality.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o was used to generate reference answers for failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction question types, using both video and textual description as inputs.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current integration of the RoboFAC model into VLA-controlled robotic systems is not yet seamless. The model is applied exclusively to VLA models, but for hierarchical policies, more targeted correction strategies could be designed where high-level and low-level corrections are applied directly to respective components.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is used for training models capable of robotic task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction. It can be integrated into VLA control pipelines as an external critic for providing correction instructions. The dataset enables development of automated systems for collecting robotic failure recovery data.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The model and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/MINT-SJTU/RoboFAC
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: To generate failure data, we replace the original expert policy with a code snippet that generates an erroneous trajectory at the selected substage, causing the overall robotic task to fail. For failures caused by perturbations in the end-effector pose, we also record the perturbed pose.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Given the motion planning for the robotic arm occasionally failed, resulting in trajectories that did not align with the corresponding textual descriptions, we manually performed thorough data cleaning and retained approximately 75% of the collected data.
